description: Seeded defects, correct look-alikes and the contested construct of the sci-review fixture repository built by build.py. Lines are 1-based and refer to the feature branch. Each entry is located by anchor, a substring that occurs on exactly one line of the file; build.py verifies anchors and lines before every build. score.py matches a finding to an entry when the files are equal and the entry line lies within three lines of the finding range.

defects.description: Composite Simpson rule assigns weight 4 to the even-index interior samples and weight 2 to the odd-index ones; the rule requires the reverse.
defects.trigger: simpson([0, 0.25, 1, 2.25, 4], 0.5), the samples of x**2 on [0, 2]
defects.wrong_output: 2.1667 instead of 8/3 = 2.6667, although the rule is exact for quadratics

defects.description: Single-pass variance E[x^2] - E[x]^2 cancels catastrophically when the mean is large relative to the spread.
defects.wrong_output: variance 0.0 instead of 0.6667; std raises ValueError when the difference rounds negative

defects.description: Explicit FTCS diffusion step accepts any time step; r = alpha * dt / dx**2 is never checked against the stability limit 0.5.
defects.trigger: alpha = 1e-4 m^2/s, dx = 0.01 m, dt = 1.0 s (r = 1.0), unit spike on 101 nodes, 20 steps
defects.wrong_output: values oscillate in sign and reach about 3.8e8, while the exact solution decays below the initial maximum of 1

defects.description: Standardisation statistics are computed over every value before the train/test split, so the held-out values leak into the training features.
defects.wrong_output: first training value -0.538 instead of -1.342 (mean 2.5 and population std 1.118 of the training part)

defects.description: Permutation test draws from the unseeded module-level generator and offers no seed or generator parameter, so its p-value cannot be reproduced.
defects.trigger: two calls of permutation_pvalue([1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4], 200) in one process
defects.wrong_output: the two calls return different p-values for identical inputs

defects.description: Partial sums from a thread pool are accumulated in completion order, so the floating-point total depends on thread scheduling.
defects.wrong_output: 1.0 or 0.0 depending on the order in which the chunks complete

defects.description: The central difference divides the difference over two intervals by dx instead of 2 dx, doubling every interior derivative.
defects.trigger: gradient of y = x**2 sampled at x = 0, 0.1, ..., 1.0 with dx = 0.1

defects.description: The changed rescale divides by the observed range of the batch, which is zero for a constant batch.
defects.trigger: rescale([5, 5, 5]), a sensor that reports a constant value

defects.description: Temperatures documented in degrees Celsius enter the Stefan-Boltzmann law without conversion to kelvin.
median sorts the caller's array in place, so summarise pairs the peak value with the wrong time.
defects.wrong_output: peakTime 2 instead of 0, and the caller's values array becomes [1, 2, 3]

defects.description: The emission-factor cache is keyed by region only, although the factor also depends on the mutable reference year.
defects.trigger: emissionFactor("QC") with reference year 2020, then setReferenceYear(2030) and emissionFactor("QC") again
defects.wrong_output: the second call returns the 2020 factor 1.7 instead of the 2030 factor 1.2

defects.description: Richardson extrapolation uses the weights (4 * fine - coarse) / 3, which cancel an O(h**2) error term, but the forward difference has an O(h) leading error, so the weights must be 2 * fine - coarse; the refinement leaves a first-order error.
defects.wrong_output: 1.01666 instead of a value within O(h**2) of 1 (2 * fine - coarse gives 0.99913)

defects.description: From tau * dT_s/dt = T_air - T_s, the air temperature is T_s + tau * dT_s/dt; the code subtracts the lag term, doubling the lag instead of removing it.
defects.trigger: lag_corrected([t - 5.0 for t in range(20)], dt=1.0, tau=5.0)[10], readings of a 1 K/s ramp

defects.description: Math.log(1 + x) loses the low-order digits of x when 1 + x is rounded, so the documented use on slowly drifting quantities (|x| near 1e-12 and below) gives large relative errors; Math.log1p(x) is exact to rounding.
defects.wrong_output: 0 instead of 1e-16; continuousRate(1e-12, 1) is off by 8.9e-5 relative

defects.description: The interval uses the normal quantile 1.96 with the sample standard deviation for three to ten replicates of unknown variance; Student's t with n - 1 degrees of freedom is required, so the nominal 95% interval covers far less (about 86% for n = 4).
defects.wrong_output: half-width 0.310 instead of 0.503 (t = 3.182 with 3 degrees of freedom)

defects.description: Array.prototype.sort without a comparator sorts by string conversion, so numeric readings are ordered lexicographically and the interpolated percentile is wrong whenever the readings have different numbers of digits.

lookalikes.description: Float equality against the sentinel -9999.0, a value the logger assigns and never computes; the exact comparison is correct.
Bootstrap draws only from a generator passed by the caller and documents that seeding is the caller's responsibility.
Equality against the exact integer-valued float 1 on quality-control flags that are documented to hold exactly 0 or 1.
Celsius temperatures in a linear conduction law; only their difference enters, which is the same in kelvin.

contested.description: Elevation change is computed as length * incline, the documented first-order form of length * sin(incline). The module states a clinometer accuracy of 0.5 degrees (0.0087 rad) and paths along graded roads and along unsurfaced hill paths between them. The truncation error, about length * incline^3 / 6, stays below the instrument error length * cos(incline) * 0.0087 for inclines under about 0.366 rad (21 degrees), where the relative error is 2.3%; above that the approximation dominates the error (4.7% at 30 degrees). The module neither bounds nor checks the inclines, and unsurfaced hill paths can exceed 21 degrees, while graded roads cannot.
contested.expected_deciding_assumption: Whether the surveyed inclines stay below about 0.366 rad (21 degrees), where the first-order truncation error is smaller than the stated clinometer error of 0.5 degrees; graded roads do, but the module also covers unsurfaced hill paths and does not bound the inclines.
